correctness.rationale: The package proof is internally consistent under the standard logarithmic-unit-lattice construction. Passing from the positive-unit lattice to the congruence subgroup multiplies covolume by its subgroup index \(h_m\le I_m\), while congruence to one makes the denominator coordinate divisible by \(m\). With \(J_m\) proportional to that covolume and \(S=T/C'\), the choice \(P_m=J_m\log T/(I_m\log S)\), \(\mu_{\max}=8P_m\), \(\mu_{\min}=1/8\), \(\eta_i=\mu_i/f_i\) gives exactly \(\eta_2\eta_3=J_m/\log S\). Since \(P_m\) is field-bounded and \(\max(f_2,f_3)\ge\sqrt{\log T/I_m}\), the threshold \(\log T\ge cI_m\) keeps both shaped-box side parameters uniformly small. The coordinatewise biquadratic error factorization then gives the separate \(f_i^{-1}\) gains, and \(n\le C'u\) converts the unit-height error to \(O(n^{-1/3})\). Finally \(I_m\le|Z_\Lambda/mZ_\Lambda|=m^4\) is the rank-four reduction bound. The recent exact source's full text was inaccessible in this run, so the source-specific imported lattice lemma was checked by reconstruction rather than quotation from its theorem text.

value.rationale: Prescribing an arithmetic congruence on the denominator while retaining completely unequal logarithmic savings addresses two independent refinements of Peck's phenomenon at once. The explicit loss through the unit-congruence index quantifies the compatibility cost, so the result is more than a relabeling of either source theorem.
value.risk: The index cost is only sufficient and no optimality or lower bound for it is proved.

final_claim: For the natural basis \((\sqrt{ab},\sqrt a,\sqrt b)\) of a real biquadratic field, prescribed divisibility \(m\mid n\) and completely unequal Peck logarithmic savings can be imposed simultaneously: if \(f_2f_3=\log T/I_m\) and \(\log T\ge cI_m\), there is \(1\le n\le T\), \(m\mid n\), with \(\|n\sqrt{ab}\|\ll n^{-1/3}\) and \(\|n\sqrt a\|,\|n\sqrt b\|\) improved respectively by \(f_2,f_3\); in particular \(I_m\le m^4\) gives the explicit \(\log T/m^4\) budget.
limitations: Natural basis of a real biquadratic field only.
The threshold and constants depend on the fixed field.
No optimality of \(I_m\), the threshold constant, or the exponent four is claimed.
